public_rationale: A 2023 planning study found that renaming actions and predicates while preserving the underlying planning problem sharply reduced GPT-4's success [e1]. A separate 2023 study found that scratchpad-trained GPT-3 performed nearly perfectly within its training distribution but failed on unfamiliar, wider or deeper computation graphs [e2]. These experiments support weak generalization as a contributor to unreliable reasoning and planning in the tested configurations [e1] [e2]. The October 25, 2023 meta-learning study demonstrated human-like systematic generalization with specialized training, qualifying the scope of this support: the limitation is not an established architectural impossibility [e3].
limitations: The experiments do not establish a literal geometric boundary around training examples or demonstrate the same limitation across all configurations covered by the claim [e1] [e2].
The planning study did not directly inspect proprietary pretraining data; dependence on familiar patterns is inferred from the renaming experiment [e1].
The reasoning tests change computational width or depth, so unfamiliarity is not isolated from increased complexity [e2].
The specialized meta-learning results concern the tested compositional tasks, not reliable reasoning and planning generally [e3].

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Neural networks, at least in the configurations dominant over the last three decades, have trouble generalizing beyond the multidimensional space surrounding their training examples, and this limits their ability to reason and plan reliably.

our_interpretation: The ordinary reading is that weak generalization to unfamiliar cases contributes to reasoning and planning errors in commonly used neural networks.
I interpret the spatial language as unfamiliar distributions or combinations, not a precise geometric boundary.
This assesses configurations common by the post date. It does not assert that every neural network fails or that improvements are impossible.
The preceding three decades describe the scope of configurations, not a requirement that the limitation be demonstrated in every year.
criteria.support_condition: Controlled studies show that unfamiliar combinations or equivalent task variants substantially reduce reasoning and planning accuracy in common configurations, linking the failures to poor generalization.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Representative controlled studies show reliable transfer to unfamiliar reasoning and planning cases, and establish that the alleged generalization limitation does not explain the failures.

evidence.explanation: The surrounding experiment reports near-perfect performance within the training distribution but failure on wider or deeper reasoning graphs. Explicit intermediate-step training did not remove that transfer failure in the tested tasks.
